subject: Re: Shiny server can't find packages when they are requested from a sourced file

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Shiny server can't find packages when they are requested from a sourced file
parts:
Shiny Server runs as the "shiny" user, so whatever libraries are available to that user is what the R process will have access to.

We run as "shiny" by default for security reasons; if there's a security flaw in one of your apps and it's running as your regular user, then your user would be completely compromised.

If you really want, you can tell Shiny Server to run as your regular user by creating a custom configuration file and changing the run_as directive.


On Tue, Jul 2, 2013 at 3:27 AM, D <dmitr...@gmail.com> wrote:
Adding the missing library path with .libPaths() inside func.R is an easy fix, but why shiny server ignores one of the library paths?


On Tuesday, July 2, 2013 12:58:54 PM UTC+3, D wrote:
Update: path.package(), ran in both server.R and func.R, includes only "/usr/lib/R/library/..." paths and ignores all "/home/user/R/..." paths that I see when running path.package() in R studio.


On Tuesday, July 2, 2013 12:33:54 PM UTC+3, D wrote:
I have shiny server running on Ubuntu 12.04. When I require() packages directly from server.R it works like a charm. However, when I source() a file in server.R, which has require() commands in it, I get a "there is no package called ..." error.

Example:
adding "require(quantmod)" directly to server.R works
adding "require(quantmod)" to  /var/shiny-server/www/func.R and then "source('/var/shiny-server/www/func.R')" to  server.R gives an error

Are there any ideas how to fix it?
